title: Elijah Calls Down Fire on Ahaziah's Captains
summary: Injured and sick, Ahaziah sends messengers to inquire of Baal-zebub, but Elijah intercepts them with a death sentence from the LORD, then calls down fire on two captains sent to arrest him before repeating the verdict to Ahaziah's face.
blurb: Fire from heaven consumes Ahaziah's captains

title: Elijah Taken Up; Elisha's Mantle
summary: Elijah is swept up to heaven in a whirlwind of fire after crossing the Jordan with Elisha, who inherits his cloak, parts the Jordan with it, heals Jericho's bad water with salt, and curses jeering boys at Bethel.
blurb: Elijah ascends; Elisha inherits his mantle

title: The Campaign Against Moab
summary: When Moab rebels, Joram of Israel marches out with Jehoshaphat of Judah and Edom's king, and after Elisha's water miracle saves their thirsty army, they rout Moab, though Mesha's desperate sacrifice of his son ends the campaign.
blurb: Elisha's water miracle wins the Moab campaign

title: Elisha's Miracles for the Prophets and a Shunammite Family
summary: Elisha multiplies a widow's oil to pay her debts, promises a childless Shunammite woman a son and later raises him from death, makes a pot of poisonous stew safe, and feeds a hundred men with twenty loaves.
blurb: Widow's oil, the Shunammite's son raised, feeding a hundred

title: Naaman Healed of Leprosy
summary: Naaman, Syria's army commander, is angered by Elisha's simple instruction to wash seven times in the Jordan, but obeys and is healed, confessing the LORD as God; his servant Gehazi secretly extorts payment and is struck with his leprosy instead.
blurb: Naaman healed; Gehazi's greed and leprosy

title: The Floating Axe Head and the Siege of Samaria
summary: Elisha makes a borrowed axe head float, then leads a blinded Syrian raiding party sent to seize him safely into Samaria; later Ben-hadad besieges the city until famine drives it to cannibalism and the king vows to kill Elisha.
blurb: Axe head floats; siege brings famine to Samaria

title: Four Lepers Discover the Abandoned Syrian Camp
summary: Elisha promises cheap food in besieged Samaria within a day, a promise a royal officer doubts; the LORD routs the Syrian army in the night, and four starving lepers discover their abandoned camp, ending the siege exactly as foretold.
blurb: Lepers find the Syrians' abandoned camp

title: The Shunammite's Land, Hazael, and Judah's Kings
summary: The Shunammite's land is restored after seven years away, Elisha weeps over Hazael's coming cruelty before Hazael murders Ben-hadad to become king of Syria, and Judah's throne passes through the evil reigns of Jehoram and his son Ahaziah.
blurb: Hazael murders Ben-hadad; Judah's kings turn evil

title: Jehu Anointed; Joram, Ahaziah, and Jezebel Killed
summary: Elisha's servant secretly anoints Jehu king of Israel to destroy Ahab's house; Jehu shoots Joram dead on Naboth's plot of ground, pursues and kills Ahaziah of Judah, and has Jezebel thrown from her window to be eaten by dogs.
blurb: Jehu kills Joram, Ahaziah, and Jezebel

title: Jehu Wipes Out Ahab's House and Baal Worship
summary: Jehu has Ahab's seventy sons beheaded and kills everyone left of his house, then tricks Baal's worshipers into a fatal assembly; yet Jehu keeps Jeroboam's golden calves, and the LORD begins letting Israel's territory be cut away.
blurb: Jehu tricks and kills the worshipers of Baal

title: Athaliah's Coup and Joash's Coronation
summary: When Ahaziah dies, Athaliah destroys Judah's royal family and seizes the throne, but the infant Joash is hidden in the temple for six years until the priest Jehoiada crowns him king and has Athaliah put to death.
blurb: Joash crowned; Athaliah's coup ends

title: Joash Repairs the Temple
summary: Joash sets up a chest to collect money for repairing the temple, which honest workmen restore with no accounting required; but when Hazael threatens Jerusalem, Joash strips the treasuries to buy him off, and is later assassinated by his own servants.
blurb: Joash's temple chest, then his assassination

title: Elisha's Death and Final Miracles
summary: As Elisha lies dying, Jehoash weeps over him and shoots an arrow of promised victory but stops short of striking the ground enough times for total triumph; after Elisha dies, a dead man revives at the touch of his bones.
blurb: Elisha's arrow of victory and his bones revive a man

title: Amaziah's Pride and Jeroboam II's Expansion
summary: Amaziah of Judah defeats Edom but is defeated and captured after foolishly challenging Jehoash of Israel to battle, and is later assassinated; Jeroboam II restores Israel's borders, fulfilling a word the LORD spoke through the prophet Jonah.
blurb: Amaziah's fall; Jeroboam II expands Israel

title: Israel's Kings Fall in Rapid Succession
summary: Azariah of Judah is struck with leprosy and hands governing to his son Jotham, while in Israel one assassination follows another until Assyria's Tiglath-pileser begins carrying off Israelite territory and people during Pekah's reign.
blurb: A chain of assassinations grips Israel's throne

title: Ahaz Appeals to Assyria
summary: Under attack from Syria and Israel, Ahaz strips the temple treasury to buy Assyria's help rather than trust the LORD, and after seeing a pagan altar in Damascus, has a copy installed in the temple as the main altar.
blurb: Ahaz buys Assyria's help, copies a pagan altar

title: The Fall of Samaria and Israel's Exile
summary: Hoshea's rebellion against Assyria ends in Samaria's fall and Israel's deportation; the text explains that persistent idolatry despite every prophet's warning is why the LORD removed Israel, and Assyria resettles Samaria with peoples who adopt a mixed worship.
blurb: Samaria falls; the reasons for Israel's exile

title: Hezekiah's Reforms and Sennacherib's Threat
summary: Hezekiah trusts the LORD more than any king of Judah, destroying even the bronze serpent Moses made, but Sennacherib of Assyria invades anyway, and after Hezekiah pays tribute, his officer the Rabshakeh mocks the LORD outside Jerusalem's wall.
blurb: The Rabshakeh mocks the LORD outside Jerusalem

title: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Assyrian Army's Destruction
summary: Hezekiah spreads Sennacherib's threatening letter before the LORD in prayer, and Isaiah answers with a promise of deliverance; that night the angel of the LORD strikes down 185,000 Assyrian soldiers, and Sennacherib is later assassinated by his own sons.
blurb: The angel of the LORD destroys Sennacherib's army

title: Hezekiah's Illness and the Babylonian Envoys
summary: Hezekiah prays when told he will die, and the LORD adds fifteen years to his life, confirmed by the sun's shadow moving backward; but when he proudly shows Babylonian envoys his treasures, Isaiah warns they will one day be carried off.
blurb: Hezekiah healed; Babylon's envoys foreshadow exile

title: Manasseh's Idolatry and Amon's Brief Reign
summary: Manasseh reverses Hezekiah's reforms, sacrifices his own son, and fills Jerusalem with innocent blood, provoking a prophetic sentence that the LORD will wipe Jerusalem out like a dish; his son Amon follows the same path before his servants assassinate him.
blurb: Manasseh's idolatry draws judgment on Jerusalem

title: The Book of the Law Found
summary: While Josiah has the temple repaired, Hilkiah discovers the Book of the Law, and Josiah tears his clothes on hearing it read; the prophetess Huldah confirms disaster is coming on Judah but promises Josiah he will die in peace first.
blurb: The Book of the Law found; Huldah's prophecy

title: Josiah's Reforms and Death
summary: Josiah renews the covenant and leads a sweeping reform, destroying idols and high places across Judah, and keeps a Passover unmatched since the judges; he is killed at Megiddo by Pharaoh Neco, who deposes Jehoahaz and installs Jehoiakim.
blurb: Josiah's reforms, great Passover, and death at Megiddo

title: Babylon's First Deportations
summary: Nebuchadnezzar subdues Jehoiakim and later besieges Jerusalem under his son Jehoiachin, who surrenders after three months and is deported along with Jerusalem's officials, soldiers, and craftsmen; Nebuchadnezzar installs Jehoiachin's uncle Zedekiah, who eventually rebels against Babylon.
blurb: Jehoiachin deported; Zedekiah installed and rebels

title: The Fall of Jerusalem
summary: Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem until famine breaks it, kills Zedekiah's sons before his eyes and blinds him, and burns the temple and palace; Gedaliah is soon assassinated, but decades later Jehoiachin is freed and honored at the Babylonian king's table.
blurb: Jerusalem falls; the temple is burned
